correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier integration and universal circle positive-type characterization reduce all finite Gram constraints to squared-sine ratios. Irrational boundedness extends a dense cyclic map to a continuous circle character, giving an iff and sharp winding-number constant; rational Fourier zeros force a finite residue test. The sum of nonzero Fourier coefficients proves the zero mode is slack. An explicit 2Q-grid null vector and a Vandermonde argument settle rational versus irrational strictness. Density and the vanishing \(k^{-2}\) spike heights prove continuity assertions. 84,177 supplementary checks passed; they are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new contribution is the all-parameter iff subgroup rigidity for positive signed two-radius subtraction, the sharp rational and irrational coefficients, and the strictness/popcorn dichotomy. Classical tent Fourier coefficients, Bochner positivity, and character structure are prior ingredients, not independently claimed as new. Read primary articles do not establish the joint theorem; unresolved earlier dilation-order and periodic-spline priority remains a risk.
residual_risks: Equivalently framed older spline-dilation inequalities or Fourier multiplier order theorems could imply the subgroup rigidity; no exhaustive historical priority certificate is asserted.
General positive-type and circle character theorems are standard; the originality claim is limited to their exact two-tent synthesis and sharp full classification.

value.rationale: For two canonical compact covariance tapers, the useful question of subtracting short-range correlation while preserving positive type receives an exact all-parameter solution. A countable dense admissible scale set, the rational/irrational change of strictness, a sharp finite trigonometric test, and the discontinuity law reveal non-obvious arithmetic constraints that cannot be replaced by numerical samples or generic positivity criteria.
